candidates.failure_reason: U113 Part III: the Chabauty-Coleman route bounds the WRONG OBJECT. U99 proves rank_Z J^-(k) <= 2 < g = 8 over k = Q(sqrt5), giving #C^-(k) <= 9. But U105 own "degree obstruction" shows a positive integer solution yields c = i*2^(4/5), whose minimal polynomial is x^10 + 256 (verified exactly), of degree 10 over k. Solutions therefore give points of C^-(L) with [L:k] = 10, which are not elements of C^-(k). A bound on the k-rational points is silent about them, so "C^-(k) contains no points from solutions, therefore no solutions" is a non sequitur with a vacuously true premise. Closing this needs Chabauty over L (degree 20 over Q) with rank_Z J^-(L) < 8 RE-ESTABLISHED (ranks grow in extensions), or symmetric-power Chabauty / covering collections. None exists in U99, U102 or U105.

If A^3+B^4=n^r, or A^3+n^r=C^4, then dividing by n^{6j} (r=6j+e, e in {1,5}) gives a rational point on the Mordell curve y^2=x^3+n^e; if A^4+n^r=C^3 the point lies on y^2=x^3-n^e. When the curve has rank 0 the point is torsion, hence integral (Nagell-Lutz), forcing n^{2j} | A, impossible for gcd(A,n)=1, n>=2, j>=1. PARI 2-descent upper bounds (unconditional) for 2<=n<=120: rank 0 for 40/119 bases (+n, r=1 mod 6), 56/119 (+n^5, r=5 mod 6), 48/119 (-n, r=1 mod 6), 66/119 (-n^5, r=5 mod 6). C177 said EulerDescentStep needs 'a few hundred lines' because mathlib has three_pid (IsPrincipalIdealRing for the ring of integers of Q(zeta_3)). That is necessary but NOT sufficient, and the missing piece is the classical trap in this exact descent. The norm form of Z[omega] is a^2 - ab + b^2, not a^2 + 3b^2. Exact identity, verified over |p|,|q| <= 25 with zero mismatches: p + q*sqrt(-3) = (p+q) + 2q*omega, so p^2 + 3q^2 = N_omega(p+q, 2q) -- whose SECOND coordinate is always EVEN. Z[sqrt(-3)] sits inside Z[omega] with index 2, and a factorisation valid in Z[omega] does not descend without a parity argument. Witness: N_omega(1,1) = 1, but (1,1) is not of the form ((p+q), 2q) for any integers p,q. So the formalisation needs the index-2 bookkeeping on top of the UFD property, and 'a few hundred lines' should be read as a LOWER BOUND. This is also exactly why the naive Euler descent in Z[sqrt(-3)] is unsound -- the historical flaw in Euler's own argument, which PSS mention in passing ('Euler's argument had a flaw, but it was later fixed by others').

candidates.claim: RESTART into the survey's other live direction, effective Diophantine geometry, with its cost computed before entry. For a fixed hyperbolic signature the Darmon-Granville curve is a Galois cover of P^1 branched over {0,1,inf} with ramification (x,y,z), and Riemann-Hurwitz gives g = 1 + N|chi|/2. Over the Beal range the genus is UNBOUNDED: with N = lcm(x,y,z) as a degree proxy, g ranges from 15/2 at (3,4,5) to 1705 at (13,17,19) for exponents <= 19, and fixing (3,4,r) gives g >= 49855/2 already at r = 9973.

candidates.evidence: Controls: (3,3,3) is the unique Beal signature with |chi| = 0 -- euclidean, not hyperbolic, and it is FLT3; the smallest POSITIVE |chi| in the Beal range is 1/12 at (3,3,4), against 1/42 at (2,3,7) for Fermat-Catalan, so the exponent-2 cases are the geometrically hard ones and Beal excludes them. MY FIRST RUN ASSERTED 1/12 WITHOUT EXCLUDING THE EUCLIDEAN CASE AND FAILED; the assertion caught it. That is preserved in the script's comments.
candidates.failure_reason: BLOCKED, and blocked DIFFERENTLY from the automorphy line. Faltings gives finiteness per signature but ineffectively; making it effective is open even for a single curve of genus >= 2 in general, and Beal needs it for infinitely many curves whose genus grows without bound, plus control of the twists. Automorphy (C171/C174) fails on the RANK of one object; this fails on UNIFORMITY over a growing family. Different walls, neither reachable at $0.
candidates.obligations: The degree proxy N = lcm(x,y,z) is a LOWER-BOUND stand-in for the actual minimal Galois cover degree; the true degree is at least this, so the genus bound is a lower bound and the unboundedness conclusion is safe, but the exact degrees are not computed here. The count and arithmetic of the TWISTS, which is where the class-group input enters, is not computed at all. Neither gap affects the unboundedness.

candidates.method: Non-abelian Hodge theory (Simpson), parabolic Higgs bundles, Hitchin-Kobayashi correspondence, harmonic maps.
obligations: Audit whether harmonic metric rigidity can bound integer points without moduli degeneration.
candidates.failure_reason: Simpson correspondence is transcendental over C, classifying representations up to complex conjugacy; the moduli space of Higgs bundles M_{Higgs} is non-compact, and the harmonic metric degenerates as lambda -> {0, 1, oo}, remaining blind to Q-rationality and Fermat-Catalan blind (U141).
candidates.novelty_note: Explores Simpson non-abelian Hodge theory and parabolic Higgs bundles for Beal triangle orbifolds.
extracted: Moduli of stable parabolic Higgs bundles is diffeomorphic to character varieties over C; harmonic metric degenerates at boundary cusps.

candidates.title: ALGEBRAIC & TRANSCENDENTAL BRAUER-MANIN OBSTRUCTIONS ON FERMAT HYPERSURFACES
candidates.claim: The Brauer group Br(X) / Br(Q) of the generalized Fermat hypersurface X: A^x + B^y = C^z over Q creates an unramified Brauer-Manin obstruction to integral points.
candidates.method: Brauer-Manin obstruction (Manin, Colliot-Thelene, Skorobogatov), unramified cohomology H^2_{nr}(X, G_m), quaternion algebras.
obligations: Audit whether Brauer-Manin obstructions can detect integer coprimality.
candidates.failure_reason: For smooth projective hypersurfaces X in P^n of dimension >= 2, the Picard group Pic(X_bar) = Z H by the Lefschetz hyperplane theorem, so the algebraic Brauer group Br_1(X) / Br(Q) = 0; transcendental Brauer classes are torsion and invariant under scaling gcd(A, B, C) > 1 (Failure Mode 1).
candidates.novelty_note: Applies Brauer-Manin obstruction to generalized Fermat hypersurfaces.
extracted: Lefschetz hyperplane theorem implies Pic(X_bar) = Z, forcing Br_1(X)/Br(Q) = 0; Brauer-Manin cannot distinguish coprime from non-coprime integer points.

candidates.title: TOPOLOGICAL HOCHSCHILD & CYCLOTOMIC TRACE MAPS OVER THE SPHERE SPECTRUM

candidates.method: Topological Hochschild homology (THH), topological cyclic homology (TC), cyclotomic trace, and higher algebra over the sphere spectrum S.
obligations: Audit whether topological cyclic homology can detect discrete naive integer heights.
candidates.failure_reason: K-theory and TC of rings of integers are finitely generated abelian groups whose higher groups K_n(Z[1/6]) are finite torsion for n >= 1 (except K_0 = Z); discrete height growth and coprime integers cannot be detected by torsion homotopy groups (Failure Mode 3).
candidates.novelty_note: Analyzes cyclotomic trace and TC(Z[1/6]) over the sphere spectrum.
extracted: K_n(Z[1/6]) is finite torsion for n >= 1; topological cyclic homology computes algebraic K-theory but cannot detect coordinate heights.
